sections.heading: Landlord Property Maintenance Obligations in Salisbury
sections.body: Landlords letting property in Salisbury and Wiltshire operate under a specific legal maintenance framework. Section 11 of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985 requires the landlord to keep the structure and exterior of the property in repair (roof, walls, foundations, windows, and external doors) and to maintain the installations for heating, hot water, gas, electricity, and sanitation. The Homes (Fitness for Human Habitation) Act 2018 extends this to 28 defined hazard categories including damp and mould growth, excess cold, structural collapse risk, and inadequate fire safety. These hazards must be absent throughout the entire tenancy, not merely at the point of letting. Electrical Installation Condition Reports (EICRs) are mandatory every five years for all privately rented properties in England. Gas Safety Certificates must be renewed annually. FixWell Services carries out the physical maintenance work required to satisfy these obligations (property inspections, repairs, condition documentation) while advising when a Gas Safe engineer or certified electrician is required for compliance-specific work.

sections.heading: Between-Tenancy Property Preparation in Salisbury
sections.body: The period between one tenant vacating and the next tenant moving in is the most concentrated maintenance window in the rental cycle. FixWell Services manages the full between-tenancy preparation process for Salisbury landlords: minor repairs to walls, floors, and fixtures identified during the check-out inspection; repainting scuffed or marked walls and woodwork with appropriate finishes; checking all door and window locks and hinges for correct operation; inspecting carpets and hard flooring for damage beyond fair wear and tear; testing all electrical switches, sockets, and light fittings; running all taps and flushing toilets to confirm plumbing function; and completing a written condition record to support the new tenancy inventory. The target window for a standard two-bedroom Salisbury terrace is three to five working days. Minimising the void period between tenants directly reduces rental income loss. A one-week reduction in the void period on a £1,000/month Salisbury rental represents £250 recovered.

sections.heading: Routine and Emergency Maintenance for Rental Properties in Salisbury
sections.body: Once a tenancy is in place, maintenance divides between planned and reactive. Planned maintenance (quarterly or annual property checks) allows FixWell Services to inspect the property condition and carry out minor repairs before they escalate into emergency callouts. Reactive maintenance handles tenant-reported faults: a dripping tap, a sticking door, a broken window catch, a blocked waste, or a failed light fitting. For emergencies (burst pipes, broken locks, or heating failure in winter), FixWell Services operates same-day attendance across Salisbury and the SP postcode area, seven days per week. Landlords and letting agents in Salisbury can add FixWell Services directly to their approved contractor list; tenants can be given the number to call directly for maintenance requests, with all work reported back to the landlord or agent after each visit.

sections.body: Salisbury's rental market is diverse: student and young professional lets concentrated in SP1 near the city centre and Salisbury College, military accommodation support near Tidworth (SP9) and Larkhill, long-term family lets in the SP2, SP4, and SP5 postcode areas, and higher-value properties in the Wiltshire villages served by Salisbury's employment base. sections.heading: What Happens If Landlord Maintenance Is Delayed in Salisbury?
sections.body: Delayed maintenance on a rental property in Salisbury creates a cascade of consequences that escalates in cost the longer the delay continues. A minor plumbing drip ignored for two months becomes a saturated floor joist and a mould outbreak, triggering a Homes (Fitness for Human Habitation) Act complaint from the tenant. A broken window catch left unrepaired becomes a basis for a deposit dispute at the end of the tenancy. Repeated maintenance failures expose a Salisbury landlord to a Section 21 restriction under the Deregulation Act 2015. A valid Section 21 notice cannot be served if there is an outstanding local authority improvement notice relating to housing conditions. FixWell Services provides the documentation trail (condition reports, repair records, and photographs) that demonstrates proactive maintenance management, which is the landlord's primary protection in housing tribunal proceedings.
